Pixel FAQ

Frequently asked questions about our pixel-perfect world.

FAQ

  • A pixel is the smallest controllable element of a picture on a screen. It's a tiny square of color that, together with many others, forms the images you see.

  • Pixel art is created on a low-resolution grid. Each pixel is a visible square, so edges appear stepped or blocky. This is a deliberate aesthetic that gives retro games their charm.

  • Common resolutions include 16×16, 32×32, and 64×64 pixels. The best choice depends on the detail you need and the final display size. Keep it small for a crisp, authentic look.

  • Yes, but limited palettes (e.g., 8–16 colors) are typical for retro pixel art. They force you to be creative and keep the artwork cohesive. Modern tools let you define custom palettes easily.

  • Always scale pixel art by integer factors (2×, 3×, etc.) and disable image smoothing. Use nearest-neighbor scaling to avoid blurry edges and preserve the crisp pixel grid.

# Pixel FAQ

A pixel-themed FAQ page built with plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. No external dependencies, no network requests, fully offline.

## Features

- 5 frequently asked questions about pixel art
- Click a question to expand its answer and collapse any other open one
- Arrow indicator rotates to show open state
- "Expand all" and "Collapse all" buttons
- Keyboard accessible: Tab to focus, Enter/Space to activate
- Visible hover, focus, and pressed states
- Responsive layout down to 360px wide
- Retro pixel-pattern background using pure CSS

## Run

Open `index.html` in any modern browser. No build step or server required.

## Files

- `index.html` — page structure and content
- `styles.css` — theming, layout, and states
- `script.js` — accordion logic
- `README.md` — this file
